Frame_1: The liquid washing up is yet to be dispensed from its container, which is being held in a poised position over a sponge. The sponge, appearing dry and ready to absorb, waits to receive the liquid. There is an anticipation in the scene as the liquid remains enclosed in its container, suggesting that the act of dispensing is imminent.
Frame_2: Now, the liquid washing up is being actively applied onto the sponge. The stream of the liquid can be discerned as it makes contact with the sponge, creating a wet spot. This wet spot reflects light differently than the rest of the sponge, indicating that the sponge is beginning to absorb the liquid.
Frame_3: The dispensing action seems to have concluded, with a discernible portion of the sponge now saturated with the liquid washing up. The wetted area appears glossier and darker in contrast to the other parts of the sponge, suggesting that a significant amount of liquid has been absorbed.
State_change_caption: Over the course of the three frames, the liquid washing up undergoes a transition from containment to dispersion. Initially, it remains securely inside its container, showing no interaction with the external environment. As the moments progress, the liquid is actively dispensed, changing its state from static to dynamic, and interacts directly with the sponge. By the final frame, it has been transferred and absorbed, transforming the visual and textural state of the sponge from dry to damp. This progression showcases the utility of the liquid washing up and its intended purpose.
